- "A grey Manxman, an old sepulchral man popularly invested with preternatural powers of discernment, insinuated that if ever Captain Ahab should be tranquilly laid out…" — The source has a two-part structure: first the Gay-Head Indian asserts a 40-year-old branding, *then* the Manxman's insinuation is presented as inferentially negating that. The draft cuts the Gay-Head Indian's claim entirely, retaining only the Manxman's statement — but without any "yet" / "however" or contrasting claim to negate, the Manxman's sentence stands on its own without structural damage; it simply asserts his view. The pivot in the source ("Yet, this wild hint seemed inferentially negatived, by what a grey Manxman insinuated") is gone, but the Manxman sentence in the draft is not a broken pivot — it has no connective implying a prior side. No finding.
- The Gay-Head Indian quotation: "Aye, he was dismasted off Japan," said an old Gay-Head Indian — in the source, this is attributed to "the old Gay-Head Indian once," referring back to "Tashtego's senior, an old Gay-Head Indian among the crew." The draft cuts Tashtego's senior / the Gay-Head Indian's prior introduction entirely. The draft sentence reads: *"said an old Gay-Head Indian"* — this is an indefinite ("an"), so the reader is not sent looking for a previously established person. The descriptor "old Gay-Head Indian" is self-identifying. Not a finding.

Is Stubb a "major or continuously present character"? Yes — he is one of the three named mates already mentioned in Ch 031 draft ("the three chief officers of the ship, the mates"). Not a finding.

The draft replaces this with an impersonal "They say," so there is no dangling reference to a removed character. The authorized removal of Dough-Boy is handled. Not a finding.
- "what does he go into the after hold for, every night?" — In the source this is "every night, as Dough-Boy tells me he suspects." Draft removes the attribution. Again, properly handled. Not a finding.

- No mid-scene jumps between Ch 031 draft and Ch 032 draft.
